t: In front of you is the Whiting Fountain, a Grade II listed drinking fountain in Guilford Place. It dates from about 1870. It was built for the Misses Whiting, who put it up to commemorate their mother. The architect was Henry Darbishire. He is best known for philanthropic schemes. He worked on projects for Angela Burdett-Coutts, and from 1863 until 1885 he was architect to the Peabody Trust. A public drinking fountain fits that charitable tradition well.
